claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index and official Army bulk record agree in exact name and a nonshared protected identifier.

claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record establishes wartime military identity but not a pre-service employer.

research_attempts.query_text: George R Moore; Pfc; OSS; employer; occupation; obituary; directory
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Library of Congress discovery items were name-only OCR hits or postwar items without an OSS, rank or grade, protected-identifier, or archival bridge.
research_attempts.research_notes: The minimum staged protocol covered the official index, a CIA Reading Room domain check, exact-name OSS searches, employment and occupation searches, a live Library of Congress newspaper query, and institutional, obituary, directory, and archival discovery checks. Official Army bulk data supplies a high-confidence identity bridge, but its coded occupation was neither published nor used as employer evidence. The direct CIA adapter failed closed once; targeted public CIA-domain review substituted, and the adapter error was not treated as negative evidence.
research_attempts.next_action: Inspect Box 534 for the personnel file and last civilian employer.
